title: Geometry-Constrained Bidirectional Point Cloud Registration for Thin, Sheet-Like Heritage Artifacts
abstract: Non-contact three-dimensional reconstruction of thin, sheet-like heritage artifacts poses significant geometric and registration challenges. Due to their fragility, these artifacts cannot be suspended or equipped with artificial markers, necessitating independent acquisition of their front and back surfaces. Subsequent registration proves difficult due to the limited number of shared geometric features and the scarcity of explicit physical constraints, which may result in rotational ambiguity, instability, and structural collapse during iterative optimization. To address these challenges, we propose a geometry-constrained bidirectional point cloud registration method specifically tailored for thin, sheet-like heritage artifacts. The method integrates semantic-guided preprocessing, Principal Component Analysis (PCA)-based geometric normalization, and a thickness-aware registration strategy. The estimated physical thickness is incorporated as a geometric constraint to preserve structural integrity during registration. Rotational ambiguity is resolved by evaluating a finite set of global rotation hypotheses, each refined using the point-to-plane Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm, with the optimal transformation selected via a geometry-aware fitness criterion consistent with the thickness scale. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves competitive or improved performance in most cases, particularly in projected area consistency and physically plausible front-back alignment. In addition, the thickness-aware constraint and rotation hypothesis evaluation reduce the risk of degenerate configurations in which the two surfaces are incorrectly flipped while still yielding deceptively acceptable numerical scores, supporting reliable non-contact digitization of delicate and thin heritage artifacts. Implementation details are available at https://zyz-nwpu.github.io/GCBPCR/.

title: EVALUATING THE ACCURACY OF MACHINE TRANSLATION BETWEEN ENGLISH AND UZBEK: A COMPUTATIONAL LINGUISTICS APPROACH
abstract: Ushbu ilmiy maqolada ingliz va o‘zbek tillari o‘rtasidagi mashina tarjimasi (MT) tizimlarining aniqligi kompyuter lingvistikasi usullari orqali baholanadi. Analitik ingliz tili va agglyutinativ o‘zbek tili o‘rtasidagi tipologik nomutanosiblik sintaktik tartib, fe’l morfemalari va kelishik qo‘shimchalarini avtomatlashtirilgan tarjima qilishda jiddiy qiyinchiliklarni keltirib chiqaradi. Tadqiqotda avtomatik baholash metrikalari (BLEU, METEOR, chrF++) hamda insoniy xatoliklar tahlili (MQM) asosida neyron tarjima tizimlarining sifati ilmiy tahlil qilinadi va tarjima sifatini oshirish bo‘yicha amaliy takliflar beriladi.

title: Additional file 4 of Automated Bergmann-Kliesch Score assessment in testicular biopsies using artificial intelligence-based whole-slide image analysis: a retrospective monocentric development and validation study
abstract: Supplementary Material 4: Bland-Altman analysis of AI-derived vs. pathologist-assigned Bergmann-Kliesch Scores. Difference (AI−Reference) plotted against the mean of both scores for (A) the full evaluation cohort (n = 74) and (B) the patient-level held-out test set (n = 15). The solid blue line indicates the mean bias, the dashed red lines indicate the 95% limits of agreement (LoA; bias±1.96 SD), and shaded bands represent 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for bias and LoA. On the full cohort, bias was −0.21 (95% CI: −0.71 to 0.29) with LoA from −4.52 to 4.10. On the test set, bias was −0.18 (95% CI: −0.79 to 0.47) with narrower LoA from −2.76 to 2.40.

title: CueWIN: code and data for "Which Cue Wins? Causal Evidence on Gender Agreement in Arabic BERT Encoders"
abstract: Code, lexicon, per-item results and reproduction scripts for the paper "Which Cue Wins? Causal Evidence on Gender Agreement in Arabic BERT Encoders" (submitted to IEEE Access). Value, hidden-state and head-level patching, value zeroing, causal repair, cumulative-window and held-out cue-set analyses for AraBERTv02, CAMeLBERT-MSA, ARBERT and MARBERT, with a treebank (UD Arabic-PADT) check.

title: Rough-Torsional Agentic RAG & Decoding (RT-ARAG) Super-Elevation of Self-RAG and Guided Decoding via UROA, STCT, and Generative Game Theory
abstract: This paper presents the formal integration of the Agentic Self-Corrective Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Self-RAG, CRAG) framework with the 15 Theoretical Frameworks introduced by Seonggil Lee. By mapping static probability metrics to Universal Rough Operator Algebra (UROA) [3] and transforming linear contrastive decoding penalties into the Seonggil Theory of Complex Torsion (STCT) [1], we establish the Rough-Torsional Agentic RAG (RT-ARAG) model. This framework eliminates hallucinations natively at the topological decoding level via destructive wave interference, while governing iterative retrieval loops through Non-commutative Generative Game Theory [4].
